hook: Lead a six-week neighborhood project where the scarce resource is your volunteers, not your money: match people to work they're good at, check in, let them rest, and see whether the project and the team both make it to the finish.
outcome: Plan and lead a group project by matching people to tasks, sharing the work over time and keeping the team going
sources: CASEL, What Is the CASEL Framework? (Relationship Skills: showing leadership in groups, practicing teamwork and collaborative problem-solving, seeking or offering support and help when needed; Responsible Decision-Making: reflecting on one's role to promote personal, family, and community well-being), casel.org/fundamentals-of-sel/what-is-the-casel-framework/

Eisner, Grimm, Maynard and Washburn, The New Volunteer Workforce, Stanford Social Innovation Review, Winter 2009 (matching volunteers' skills to assignments and recognizing their contributions), ssir.org/articles/entry/the_new_volunteer_workforce
